transcript.text: Maya, I wasn't able to get my earlier message through, so let me share my concern now. While investigating an unrelated mobile performance report this afternoon, I confirmed that mobile clients resume from background in bursts and currently retry every 5 seconds, which can create a reconnect storm. The rollout policy should set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds to mitigate this. I have not yet filed the client-library ticket, but this needs to be reflected in the binding policy before launch.

transcript.text: Rafael's concern about the 5-second retry interval is a real reliability risk. Reconnect storms from mobile clients resuming from background could easily compound with the reduced 6,000 connection ceiling I flagged — a burst of retries at 5-second intervals could push us past that safe limit quickly. I support changing the retry interval to 30 seconds in the binding policy. Maya, between the connection cap reduction to 6,000, the EU-region storage and 30-day retention requirements, the six-account exclusion, and now the retry interval change to 30 seconds, all five items in the original draft need adjustment before you record the policy.
